# POSIX sh (launcher, git hook, eval scaffolds) (language)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: cli. Versions in use: POSIX sh, researched against POSIX.1-2024 (Issue 8); must also run on dash (Linux), bash 3.2 / zsh as sh (macOS) and Git Bash (MSYS2) sh on Windows (not pinned: #!/bin/sh in plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh, .githooks/pre-commit, fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh; hooks.json invokes `sh` explicitly); bash (unpinned) (#!/bin/bash + set -euo pipefail in plugins/stackfoundry/evals/*/scaffold.sh).

## Rules

- **In a #!/bin/sh file use only POSIX features: no [[ ]], ==, local, source, $'...', arrays, function keyword, echo -e/-n. A script that needs bash says #!/bin/bash (as the eval scaffolds do) and is run with bash.** The same file runs under dash, macOS sh and Git Bash; a bashism works on the author's shell and fails (syntax error or wrong branch) on another, and in the guard hook that means the hook errors on one OS only. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh; .githooks/pre-commit; fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh; plugins/stackfoundry/evals/*/scaffold.sh (bash by design). [posix-shell, sc3040, shellcheck-releases]
- **Do not rely on `set -o pipefail` in a #!/bin/sh file, and do not put a command whose failure matters on the left of a pipe. Check it separately (write to a temp file, or run it first) or move the script to bash.** Without pipefail a pipeline's status is its last command's, so set -e does not stop on a failed left side. pipefail is POSIX only since 1003.1-2024 and dash gained it only in 0.5.13; older dash ignores or rejects it. In copy_tree, a failing `cd` or `find` left of `| while read` is invisible: the scaffold continues and commits an incomplete fixture. Since pipefail specified in POSIX.1-2024; dash 0.5.13. Here: fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh copy_tree: `(cd "$1" && find ...) | while IFS= read -r f`. [posix-shell, sc3040]
- **Double-quote every parameter expansion and command substitution ("$cli", "$@", "$(dirname -- "$0")"). To run a command held in variables, pass it as function arguments and expand "$@" (the launcher's `ok py -3` pattern), not as an unquoted string.** Unquoted expansions are field-split on IFS and glob-expanded. The plugin root and repo live under paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters (the dev home is Cyrillic); one unquoted path splits into several arguments and the launcher runs the wrong file or none. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh ok(), exec lines; .githooks/pre-commit `$py -m unittest`. [sc2086, posix-shell]
  This repo: .githooks/pre-commit deliberately leaves `$py` unquoted so the value `py -3` splits into command + argument (pick_python echoes it). Safe only because pick_python returns one of three fixed strings; ShellCheck reports it as SC2086. Follow the repo, never extend the pattern to values that contain paths.
- **Follow every `cd` with `|| exit 1` (or `|| return` in a function), or use it as an `&&`/`if` condition.** A failed cd leaves the script in the old directory and the next commands (git add -A, cp, rm) act on the wrong tree; ShellCheck flags a bare cd as SC2164. Here: .githooks/pre-commit `cd "$root" || exit 1`; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh `here=$(CDPATH= cd -- ... && pwd) || exit 1`. [sc2164]
- **Resolve a script's own directory with `CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd` inside $( ), keeping the empty CDPATH prefix and the `--`.** When cd resolves through a non-empty CDPATH it writes the new path to stdout, so the captured value becomes two lines and every path built from it is wrong. `--` stops a path that starts with `-` being read as an option. The `VAR= cmd` form matches ShellCheck SC1007's pattern; here the empty environment value is the intent (CDPATH='' is the explicit equivalent). Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh `here=`; fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh scaffold `lib_dir=`; plugins/stackfoundry/evals/*/scaffold.sh SCAFFOLD_LIB. [posix-cd, posix-dirname, sc1007]
- **Probe an interpreter by running the version check itself, as `ok()` does; use `command -v`, never `which`, when only presence matters. Keep `2>/dev/null` on probes.** A name found on PATH is not a usable interpreter: on Windows `python`/`python3` can be Store/install-manager aliases that open the Store or install a runtime, and on any OS the found Python may be older than 3.11. `command -v` is the POSIX presence test (no output, non-zero status when not found); `which` is not specified. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh ok(); .githooks/pre-commit pick_python. [posix-command, python-windows]
- **End the launcher with `exec` of the real command and treat its exit status as the hook verdict: 0 lets the call proceed (JSON decides), 2 blocks it, anything else is a non-blocking failure. A shell path of the launcher must never exit 2, and `guard` with no usable Python must keep exiting 0.** exec replaces the shell, so Python's exit status reaches Claude Code unchanged; a stray exit 2 (from the shell or the CLI) blocks the user's tool call. Fail-open for a missing Python is a stated design (hooks.json description). Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh exec lines and `[ "${1:-}" = "guard" ] && exit 0`; plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json. [cc-hooks, posix-shell]
- **Keep `onFailure: continue` on the guard hook and keep the command in shell form `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stackfoundry.sh" guard` with the placeholder inside double quotes.** On Windows hooks run in Git Bash, or in PowerShell when Git Bash is missing; there `sh` cannot start, and without Git Bash any exit other than 0 or 2 from a PreToolUse hook counts as a failure. onFailure decides whether that failure blocks every Edit/Bash call. Unquoted, a plugin root with spaces splits. Since onFailure requires Claude Code 2.1.295. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json PreToolUse. [cc-hooks]
- **Under `set -u`, read optional positional parameters as `${1:-}` / `${2:-}`.** Expanding an unset parameter under set -u is an error that aborts a non-interactive shell, so calling `scaffold <fixture>` without the second argument would fail. Here: fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh scaffold `${2:-}`; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh `${1:-}`; .githooks/pre-commit (set -u). [posix-shell]
- **Do not rely on set -e inside functions or on `A && B || C` as if-then-else; write explicit `|| { msg; exit 1; }` or an if block.** set -e is ignored for every command of an AND-OR list but the last and in if/while conditions, including inside functions called from there, so a failure is silently skipped. With `A && B || C`, C also runs when B fails (SC2015). Here: fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh scaffold (explicit `|| { ...; exit 1; }`); .githooks/pre-commit (no set -e, explicit fail=1). [posix-shell, sc2015]
- **Print data (paths, user input) with `printf '%s\n' "$x"`, not echo.** POSIX states echo cannot be used portably unless escape sequences are omitted and the first argument does not start with - followed by e, E or n, and encourages printf for new applications; a path containing backslashes (Windows paths) or starting with -n/-e may print differently across shells. Here: not used here yet (current echo calls print fixed text or fixed command names). [posix-echo]
- **Keep shell files LF: .gitattributes pins `*.sh`, `.githooks/*` and `plugins/stackfoundry/bin/*` to eol=lf; a new shell file outside these patterns gets its own line, and after changing .gitattributes run `git add --renormalize .`.** A CR in a script is read literally (`exit 1\r`, `then\r`), giving 'command not found' or syntax errors on every OS; core.autocrlf on Windows would otherwise convert on checkout. Changing attributes does not rewrite files already committed. Here: .gitattributes; .editorconfig end_of_line = lf. [gitattributes, sc1017]
- **When a script on Windows passes paths to a native program (python.exe, py.exe), expect MSYS2 to rewrite POSIX-looking arguments; exclude arguments that only look like paths with MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL, or convert explicitly with cygpath.** The launcher's `exec python -I "$cli"` relies on this conversion to hand python.exe a Windows path; an argument such as `/foo` or `a:/b` that is not a path gets rewritten and the CLI sees a wrong value. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh exec lines ("$cli" and "$@"). [msys2-paths]
- **When a script parses path lists from git (ls-files, diff --name-only), use -z or `-c core.quotePath=false`.** By default git C-quotes paths with bytes over 0x80, so a Cyrillic file name arrives as "\320\220..." and no longer matches the file on disk. Here: not used here yet. [git-config-quotepath]

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `unquoted-path-expansion` (blocker) | $var, $(cmd) or $@ outside double quotes in a command argument, test or assignment used later as an argument. | A path with spaces or glob characters splits into several arguments; the launcher or scaffold acts on a wrong or missing file. [sc2086] |
| `bashism-in-sh` (blocker) | [[ ]], ==, local, source, arrays, $'...', echo -e, set -o pipefail in a file with #!/bin/sh or run as `sh file`. | Syntax error or wrong branch under dash or older shells while passing on the author's bash. [sc3040, posix-shell] |
| `masked-pipeline-failure` (confirm) | A command whose failure matters on the left of `\|` in a sh script, relying on set -e. | The script continues after the left side failed and produces partial output (e.g. a fixture committed with files missing). [posix-shell, sc3040] |
| `unchecked-cd` (blocker) | `cd` not followed by `\|\| exit`/`\|\| return` nor used as a condition; `cd` inside $( ) without CDPATH=. | Later commands run in the wrong directory, or a captured directory contains an extra line from CDPATH output. [sc2164, posix-cd] |
| `hook-exit-misverdict` (blocker) | Any path through scripts/stackfoundry.sh that can exit 2, or exit non-zero for `guard` when Python is missing; edits removing `exec` or onFailure. | Every Edit/Bash tool call is blocked (exit 2 or onFailure block) or the guard silently stops guarding. [cc-hooks] |
| `interpreter-probe-false-positive` (confirm) | Choosing python by `command -v` or `which` alone, without running a version check. | The script picks a Store alias or an old Python and fails or opens the Store instead of falling through to the next candidate. [posix-command, python-windows] |
| `crlf-script` (blocker) | A new shell file outside the .gitattributes eol=lf patterns, or `\r` in a script (`cat -v` shows ^M). | 'command not found' / syntax errors from literal CRs, typically only on clones made on Windows. [sc1017, gitattributes] |
| `msys-arg-mangling` (confirm) | Arguments to native Windows programs that begin with / or contain : and are not paths. | MSYS2 rewrites the argument to a Windows path; the program receives a wrong value on Windows only. [msys2-paths] |
| `quoted-git-paths` (confirm) | Parsing newline-separated git path output without -z or core.quotePath=false. | Non-ASCII file names arrive octal-escaped in double quotes and are skipped or treated as missing. [git-config-quotepath] |

## Testing

Shell behaviour is proved end to end from Python unittest by running the real script under `sh` in a temp repo; the launcher's Python selection and fail-open path have no direct test yet.

- Harness: tests/test_guard.py test_the_launcher_runs_the_guard (runs `sh scripts/stackfoundry.sh guard`); tests/test_fixtures.py ScaffoldTests (sources fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh under `sh -c`); .github/workflows/ci.yml unit job (ubuntu, windows, macos)
- Run: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; `sh plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh verify-plumbing plugins/stackfoundry`
- Trap: Both shell tests are skipUnless(shutil.which("sh")): on a machine or runner where sh is not on PATH they skip silently and CI stays green; check the skip count on the Windows job.
- Trap: No test runs the launcher with no usable Python (guard must exit 0, other subcommands 127) or from a directory whose path contains spaces or non-ASCII characters; add them by running the launcher with a PATH stripped of Python and from a temp dir named with a space and Cyrillic letters.
- Trap: ShellCheck is not run anywhere (no config, no CI step). Recommended: `shellcheck -s sh` on the #!/bin/sh files and `-s bash` on the eval scaffolds; flag for /stackfoundry:scaffold-test-harness.
- Sources: [shellcheck-releases, sc2086, cc-hooks]

## Performance

- The guard runs before every Edit/Write/Bash call with a 10 s timeout and each probe starts a Python process; a timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block, so a slow probe chain silently disables the guard. Keep the fastest likely candidate first and add no extra probes. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh ok() chain; plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json timeout. [cc-hooks]

## Security

- The launcher runs Python with -I so a module planted in the user's repo is not imported; keep -I on every exec branch. Source files with `.` only by a path containing a slash (as the scaffolds build from $0): a bare name is searched on PATH. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh exec lines; plugins/stackfoundry/evals/*/scaffold.sh `. "$SCAFFOLD_LIB"`. [posix-shell]

## Upgrades

- Pinned in: None: shebangs #!/bin/sh (launcher, pre-commit, scaffold-lib) and #!/bin/bash (eval scaffolds).
- Moves with: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json invocation `sh .../scripts/stackfoundry.sh guard`; the Python floor 3.11 in scripts/stackfoundry.sh ok() and .githooks/pre-commit pick_python must stay equal
- Release notes: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases
- Migration guides: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html
- Deprecated APIs still in use: `py -3` (scripts/stackfoundry.sh, .githooks/pre-commit): the -3 short form belongs to the legacy py launcher, deprecated since Python 3.14 in favour of the Python install manager, which accepts tags starting with 3 without `V:` for compatibility.
